items.title: How A.I. Is Transforming Mathematics
items.author: Max Read, Whitney Jones, Sawyer Roque, Vjeran Pavic, Chris Wood, Dan Powell, Elisheba Ittoop, Marion Lozano, Sophia Lanman and Rowan Niemisto
items.content: <article>“One thing that A.I. has done is that it’s given us answers without insight, without understanding.”</article>

items.title: Jensen Huang Is Back, and So Is His Plaque at Denny’s
items.author: Claire Moses
items.content: <article>The chain said it had restored a plaque honoring Mr. Huang above a booth in San Jose, Calif., where he is said to have developed the idea for Nvidia.</article>

items.title: Why Some A.I. Evangelists Aren’t Bothered by the Potential for Human Extinction
items.author: David Wallace-Wells
items.content: <article>Understanding the set of beliefs that drives the Silicon Valley vanguard.</article>

items.title: Nvidia Halts Sales to Southeast Asia as U.S. Tightens China Restrictions
items.author: Adam Satariano and Paul Mozur
items.content: <article>The shipping halt, which hit four countries, follows a new U.S. rule that would require licenses for companies in the countries to buy advanced A.I. chips.</article>

items.title: How to Talk to Your Family About A.I. Doom at Thanksgiving
items.author: Emmy Martin
items.content: <article>For people steeped in the world of artificial intelligence, the topic could be a minefield at this year’s dinner.</article>

items.title: A Man in Denver Has Been Throwing Eggs at Waymo Vehicles
items.author: Johnny Diaz
items.content: <article>The man, who drove a Toyota Corolla from a fleet leased to Lyft drivers, used orange cones to trap the self-driving vehicles before pelting them with eggs, the police said. No charges have been filed.</article>

items.title: Anthropic’s Stock Debut Could Hurt Tech Start-Ups
items.author: Cory Weinberg
items.content: <article>As the share price drops, it could act as a brake on Silicon Valley’s frenzied investing in younger companies.</article>

items.title: How to Use Your Apps With Fewer Taps
items.author: J. D. Biersdorfer
items.content: <article>With pop-up menus and widgets, your phone or tablet gives you quick ways to check information and get things done with less effort.</article>

items.title: The Web May Be Dying. Can Net Art Save It?
items.author: Tina Rivers Ryan and Marissa Alper
items.content: <article>A new exhibition celebrates the possibilities of net art and the vision of the pioneering Whitney Museum curator whose commissions defined the field.</article>

items.title: Blanche Downplays Questions Over Nvidia as Investigators Examine Company’s Customers
items.author: Devlin Barrett and Ana Swanson
items.content: <article>Justice Department investigators have gathered evidence of Nvidia’s high-powered computer chips being illegally diverted by other firms to China, according to people familiar with the inquiries.</article>

items.title: Jensen Huang Apologizes to Nvidia Employees, Says He Is in Therapy
items.author: Tripp Mickle and Kalley Huang
items.content: <article>A day after returning to his company, Mr. Huang acknowledged that he had violated Nvidia’s code of conduct and “made some terrible mistakes.”</article>

items.title: Trump’s Own Stock Portfolio Likely Benefits From Nvidia’s Rise
items.author: Ben Protess
items.content: <article>It’s not possible to determine the size of the president’s stake in the chip maker because there is a lag between when trades occur and when they are disclosed.</article>

items.title: OpenAI Engineer Secretly Recorded Dozens of Meetings, Prosecutors Say
items.author: Emmy Martin
items.content: <article>Abdulrahman Alfozan, who has been jailed since October, will be freed on a $1 million bond. Prosecutors say he recorded dozens of meetings.</article>

items.title: From Chinese Factory Town to the Nvidia Scandal: The Rise of Alice Huang
items.author: Paul Mozur, Keith Bradsher, Mara Hvistendahl, Michael Forsythe and Ana Swanson
items.content: <article>The woman whose role has become a focus of the Nvidia spying saga grew up in a small town built around a weapons factory. Her jump to finance and the tech world paralleled China’s own.</article>

items.title: With Jensen Huang’s Return as C.E.O., Trump Effectively Overrode Nvidia’s Board
items.author: Kalley Huang, Jordyn Holman, Lauren Hirsch and Ryan Mac
items.content: <article>Nvidia’s board said Mr. Huang would not be back. But President Trump, who pushed for Mr. Huang’s reinstatement, effectively overrode the board, governance experts said.</article>

items.title: Why Trump Put Jensen Huang Back in Charge at Nvidia
items.author: Max Read, Sawyer Roque, Vjeran Pavic, Alyssa Moxley, Chris Wood, Katie McMurran, Dan Powell, Elisheba Ittoop, Marion Lozano, Sophia Lanman and Rowan Niemisto
items.content: <article>In a shocking turn, the chip-making giant reinstated its chief executive. We unpack how it happened — and what it means.</article>

items.title: Trump’s Extraordinary Nvidia Intervention Sidelines National Security Concerns
items.author: Peter Baker
items.content: <article>President Trump’s move to put Jensen Huang back at the helm of Nvidia caps his indifference to the warnings of his own intelligence agencies.</article>

items.title: Trump Is Said to Have Pushed to Reinstate Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang
items.author: Maggie Haberman, Jonathan Swan and Julian E. Barnes
items.content: <article>The president set in motion a weekend of maneuvering, led by Vice President JD Vance, to help Jensen Huang get his old job back.</article>

items.title: Republicans Break With Trump Over Jensen Huang’s Reinstatement at Nvidia
items.author: Robert Jimison
items.content: <article>It was a rare instance of the G.O.P. pushing back on the president and threatening to use its oversight and legislative power to challenge his administration’s approach.</article>

items.title: Have You Worked With Nvidia? We Want to Hear From You.

items.title: Jensen Huang’s Return as Nvidia CEO Feels Like Déjà Vu in Silicon Valley
items.author: Cade Metz
items.content: <article>The rise, fall and return of founders of Silicon Valley tech companies is a well-worn tale.</article>

items.title: SpaceX Sued By Oregon and Virginia Over A.I.-Generated Sexualized Images
items.author: Kate Conger and Grace Kay
items.content: <article>The states accused Elon Musk’s company of violating consumer protection laws with its Grok Imagine artificial intelligence tool, which created the images.</article>

items.title: Looking for the Formula to Stop an Apocalypse
items.author: Eli Saslow and Erin Schaff
items.content: <article>Mike Winer and his colleagues are trying to build a mathematical safeguard to keep A.I. under human control. They fear they are running out of time.</article>
